title: The Secrets of a Good Speech
text:
A good speech usually begins with a short story or a surprising question. This helps the audience pay attention from the first moment. After the opening, the speaker explains the main message and gives clear reasons for it. Speakers often practise in front of a mirror or a friend before the real event.

Eye contact is one of the most important skills in public speaking. When a speaker looks at the audience, people feel more connected to the message. Nervous speakers sometimes read their notes too quickly, so they should pause and breathe. A calm voice and relaxed body language also make the speech more convincing.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, how does a good speech usually begin?
options: With a short story or a surprising question
With a list of all the speaker's notes
With a long apology to the audience
With a song performed for the audience

questions.text: What do nervous speakers sometimes do, according to the second paragraph?
options: They look only at the ceiling
They read their notes too quickly
They speak in a very loud voice

questions.text: Why might a speaker who practises in front of a friend feel more prepared?
options: They have already received feedback on the speech
They no longer need any notes at all
The audience will not be present on the day
The speech will automatically become shorter

questions.text: What can be inferred about the role of voice and body language in a speech?
options: They help make the speech more convincing
They are less important than the notes
They should be hidden from the audience
They matter only for the speaker's friends

vocabulary.definition: the people who listen to or watch a speech or performance
feeling close to or linked with someone or something
a short moment of silence before continuing
able to make people believe that something is true

paragraph_translations: Dobre przemówienie zwykle zaczyna się od krótkiej historii lub zaskakującego pytania. To pomaga publiczności skupić uwagę od pierwszej chwili. Po wstępie mówca wyjaśnia główne przesłanie i podaje jasne powody. Mówcy często ćwiczą przed lustrem lub przed przyjacielem, zanim nadejdzie prawdziwe wydarzenie.

Kontakt wzrokowy jest jedną z najważniejszych umiejętności w publicznych wystąpieniach. Gdy mówca patrzy na publiczność, ludzie czują się bardziej związani z przekazem. Zdenerwowani mówcy czasem czytają notatki zbyt szybko, dlatego powinni zrobić pauzę i oddychać. Spokojny głos i zrelaksowana mowa ciała również sprawiają, że przemówienie jest bardziej przekonujące.
